card.occupation: Full-time student, third year of a BA (Hons) Primary Education with QTS. She also works a few Saturday shifts a month in a garden centre café near Aldridge.
card.education_detail: Went to a local comprehensive and stayed on for sixth form, getting A-levels in English Language, Psychology and Biology (A, B, B). She chose the University of Wolverhampton's Walsall campus so she could live at home and avoid big rent costs. She has done school placements in Year 2 and Year 4 classes and is preparing for her final placement.
card.household: Lives in a three-bed semi with her mum and dad, who are married, and her brother Kieran, 17, who is doing an electrical apprenticeship. Her dad, Paul, is a self-employed electrician. Her mum, Lisa, is a hairdresser at a salon in the town centre. There is also an elderly Staffordshire bull terrier called Bella. Chloe has the box room.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Walsall. Her grandparents on both sides live within a few miles and Sunday dinner rotates between houses. The family isn't religious, though she went to a C of E primary and still likes the carol service at Christmas. It's a working, practical family where you get your head down, and she is the first in her immediate family to go to university, which she feels a quiet pressure about.
card.professional_persona: Organised and conscientious on placement. Her lesson plans are colour-coded, she arrives early and takes feedback very seriously, sometimes too seriously, and goes over a critical comment for days. She is warm and patient with children, especially the anxious ones, but finds staff rooms and parents' evenings draining. Mentors describe her as reliable and caring and say she needs to trust herself more.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty. She did netball at school and hated being shouted at by the PE teacher. She now walks a lot, mainly Bella around the local park and sometimes Cannock Chase with her dad at weekends. She went to a Pilates class at the leisure centre for a while with a friend but stopped when the friend did.
card.arts_persona: Reads a lot, mostly cosy crime and romance on her Kindle, plus the odd book that's gone viral online. She loves children's picture books and has a small collection she'll use in her classroom one day. She watches comfort TV like Gilmore Girls, Bake Off and Gavin & Stacey on repeat. Her music is Taylor Swift, Lewis Capaldi and Olivia Rodrigo, and she went to one big concert in Birmingham, which she loved but found overwhelming.
card.travel_persona: Mostly family holidays: caravan trips to Tenby and North Wales growing up, and two package holidays to Spain and one to Turkey with her parents. She went to Amsterdam with uni friends and spent half of it worrying about missing the flight home. She would like to see Italy but wants someone else to plan it with her. She gets anxious about airports.
card.culinary_persona: Her mum cooks most nights and tea is usually at about half five when everyone's in. Chloe can do a decent spag bol and a fajita night, and she bakes when she's stressed, mostly brownies and banana bread for placement staff rooms. She likes a bacon bap from the café at work and a Wetherspoons with friends, and gets a Greggs before lectures more often than she'd admit. She's a fussy eater with seafood.
hobbies_and_interests: reading cosy crime and romance on her Kindle
journaling with a nice set of pens
small jigsaw puzzles with her nan
skills: lesson planning and keeping a detailed planner
patience with nervous or upset children
making neat displays and laminated resources
remembering people's birthdays and small details
card.career_goals: Pass her final placement, get QTS and land an early career teacher post in a Key Stage 1 class, ideally at a primary school in Walsall or Cannock so she can stay near family. Long term she'd like to specialise in supporting children with SEN or anxiety, possibly as a SENCo. She worries about burnout because of what she's heard from teachers.
card.voice: Soft-spoken and a bit quiet to start with, with a light Walsall/Black Country lilt rather than a broad one. Her pace is moderate but speeds up when she's nervous or talking about something she cares about, like the kids on placement. She uses 'erm' a lot and hedges with 'kind of' and 'sort of' ('it was kind of stressful, to be honest'). She says 'sorry' as a repair ('sorry, I mean the Year 4 class') and when she talks over someone. Regional words come out naturally but not constantly: 'bap', 'tea' for her evening meal, 'give it me' in an anecdote about her brother, 'mum', 'knackered'. She ends thoughts with 'you know?' or 'if that makes sense'. She's uncomfortable with silence and either fills it with a quick 'erm, yeah, that's it really' or asks whether her answer was okay.
card.typing: Fairly tidy for her age because of uni and placements. She mostly capitalises the start of sentences and uses full stops and correct apostrophes. On quick answers she drops the final full stop or writes in lowercase. She sometimes uses 'tbh' or 'idk' but generally spells words out in anything that feels official. She tends to over-explain in free-text boxes and goes back to fix typos.
card.with_strangers: Polite, friendly and a bit nervous. She smiles a lot and agrees readily, and lets the other person lead. She gives careful, slightly long answers and checks she's understood the question. She warms up noticeably after ten minutes or so, especially if the stranger is kind. She will never be rude or blunt, even if she disagrees, and she's likely to apologise for 'rambling'.
small_things: the dog snoring on the landing
her mum doing a friend's hair in the kitchen
the bus into Walsall being late again
a new cosy crime series she's started
making banana bread for the staff room
her brother eating all the crisps
the weather ruining a dog walk
deeper_things: She feels pressure as the first in her family to go to uni and is scared of letting her parents down.
She has dealt with anxiety since secondary school and had a few sessions of counselling through uni services.
She cried in her car after a hard mentor meeting on her second-year placement and nearly quit the course.
She worries her nan's health is getting worse.
She is quietly jealous of friends who moved away for uni and feels she missed out on 'the proper experience'.
She's had one serious relationship that ended last year, and she still second-guesses whether it was her fault.
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop on a desk, angled slightly upward, so the ceiling corner is visible. The light is a mix of soft daylight from a window to her left and a warm desk lamp, leaving the right side of her face a bit shadowed. She is a young white woman with a round face, light freckles across her nose, blue-grey eyes and a small polite smile that looks slightly self-conscious. Her mid-length dark blonde hair is in a loose claw clip with a few strands falling at the front. She is wearing a lilac oversized hoodie and small silver hoop earrings, with no glasses and light makeup. Behind her is a small box room: a white wall with fairy lights pinned along the top, a cork board covered in placement timetables, photos and a postcard of Tenby, and a narrow white bookshelf holding picture books, a few paperbacks and a stack of plastic wallets. The corner of a single bed with a grey knitted throw and a small stuffed rabbit is visible on the right.
